rationale: Block 5 covers recurrent laryngeal nerve anatomy and vocal cord palsy — a high-yield clinical reasoning topic requiring understanding of how RLN course predicts the causative lesion.
Block 9 covers diagnosis and differential diagnosis of hoarseness, including the critical red-flag rule that persistent hoarseness beyond three weeks mandates laryngoscopy to exclude malignancy.
Block 4 covers benign structural lesions including vocal cord nodules, polyps, and papillomas — key distinguishing features are required at the Remember level.
Block 6 covers inflammatory laryngeal conditions including acute epiglottitis — a paediatric emergency requiring immediate recognition and the danger of oropharyngeal examination.
Block 4 covers anatomy, pathology and spread — the glottic vs supraglottic distinction is the single most important known-trap for EN4.42 and determines prognosis and presentation.
Block 10 covers principles of management including the prognostic superiority of glottic carcinoma — encoding the key fact about T1 glottic carcinoma radiotherapy cure rates.
Block 5 covers causes of stridor by age group — clinically organising the differential by age is the core skill of this SDL.
Block 10 covers management hierarchy of stridor, including the tracheostomy vs cricothyroidotomy decision — a key known-trap for urgent airway management.
Block 6 covers tracheostomy technique including the correct tracheal ring level — a classic known-trap distinguishing tracheostomy from cricothyroidotomy and the reason the first ring is avoided.
Block 8 covers tracheostomy care and a key distinction between tracheostomy (planned procedure at tracheal rings 2-3) and cricothyroidotomy (emergency through the cricothyroid membrane).
